summary: Satoshi Ito works in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University from circa 1980 to 1989 and was appointed professor at Ibaraki University around 2006.
Satoshi Kawano is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a doctorate in literature from the University of Tokyo. He became a professor at Kogakkan University in 2000.

Satoshi Naiki specializes in history and archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Kyoto University, where publications from 2016 to 2020 record him as Assistant Professor at the Center for Cultural Heritage Studies.

Satya Narayan Goenka worked in Buddhist and religious studies, studying under U Ba Khin from circa 1955 to 1969. He founded the Vipassana Research Institute in 1985 and taught students including Sonam Kachru, Anagarika Munindra, and Stephen Batchelor.

Satya Swarup Misra is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor and Head of the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Lucknow (attested 1958) and as Professor of Indology and Linguistics at Banaras Hindu University.

Satya Vrat Shastri was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Charu Deva Shastri, Shukdev Jha, and Siddheshwar Varma, earning degrees at University of the Punjab and Banaras Hindu University. He held professorships at University of Delhi and served as Vice-Chancellor of Shri Jagannath Sanskrit Vishvavidyalaya.

Satyendra Nath Bose studied at Hindu School, Presidency University, and the University College of Science, Technology & Agriculture. He taught at the University of Calcutta and the University of Dhaka, later serving as Vice-Chancellor of Visva-Bharati University from circa 1956 to 1958.

Sayadaw U Pandita was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Nandasiri Sayadaw and Mahasi Sayadaw. He taught at Mahasi Sasana Yeiktha, succeeded Mahasi Sayadaw from 1982 to 1991, and founded and served as abbot of the Panditarama Meditation Center.

Sayadaw U Silananda was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Sayadaw U Pannavanta and Mahasi Sayadaw, and attended University College, Colombo. He held monastic leadership roles, served as Chancellor of the International Theravāda Buddhist Missionary University (1999), and founded Dhammānanda Vihara.

Sayadaw U Thittila was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Sayadaw Ashin Adiccavamsa and at Visva-Bharati University. He served as librarian at the Adyar Library and The Buddhist Society, and was appointed Lecturer in Buddhist Philosophy at University of Rangoon in 1952.
Sayaka Sonoda is a scholar in the fields of Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at Toyo University under the supervision of Shinobu Yamaguchi.

Scott A. Mitchell specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the Graduate Theological Union under Richard K. Payne (attested 2008) and is recorded as a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies in 2015.

Scott Pacey is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies who earned his doctorate from Australian National University in 2011. He held a postdoctoral fellowship at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and later served as Lecturer at the University of Manchester.

Sean D. Gaffney is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at SOAS University of London under doctoral supervisor Tadeusz Skorupski and teachers Philip T. Denwood, Renate Söhnen-Thieme, Alexander Piatigorsky, and David Seyfort Ruegg, and held an attested post there in 1996.

Sebastian Pole works in Indology and related fields. He pursued his studies at the East West College of Herbalism, the London College of Traditional Acupuncture and Oriental Medicine, and the College of Ayurveda.
See Mui Yian is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Doctor of Philosophy from The University of Hong Kong, where the degree was supervised by K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2010).

Seema Alavi is a historian and Indologist who earned her doctorate from the University of Cambridge. She has held teaching posts at Jawaharlal Nehru University, Jamia Millia Islamia, the University of Delhi, and Ashoka University, where she became professor of history around 2020.

Seigai Omura was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Tokyo University of the Arts under Kanō Tomonobu from circa 1889 to 1893, later serving there as assistant professor in 1896 and professor in 1898.

Seiichi Mizuno was a specialist in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied under Kosaku Hamada at Kyoto University, where he earned his doctorate, worked at the Institute for Research in Humanities, and served as professor from 1949 to 1968.

Seiichi Yagi is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held academic posts at Kanto Gakuin University (circa 1960–1974), Tokyo Institute of Technology (circa 1974–1995), and Toin University of Yokohama (circa 1995–2002).
